description: Knowledge-graph judgments (wording from teacher/kg_proc.py): is a sentence's claim a fact; do two mentions or records name the same entity; how two things relate

status.instructions: Does `sentence` assert its main claim as a fact, or does it hedge, deny, project or merely propose it? Judge the modality of the sentence, not whether the claim is plausible.

criteria.asserted: The text states this relationship as a present or past fact. It holds, or it held.
criteria.hypothetical: The text raises this relationship only as a possibility, a condition, a proposal awaiting approval, or something that would happen if something else did. It is not claimed to have happened.
criteria.negated: The text denies this relationship, or states that it will not happen, is not planned, or is not expected.
criteria.forward_looking: The text projects, forecasts or guides that this relationship will hold in the future. It has not happened yet, but it is not merely conditional.

factual.instructions: If a knowledge graph recorded the relationship this sentence is about as a plain fact, would the graph be correct? Be careful with denials: a sentence saying something will NOT happen or is NOT planned does not make that thing a fact.

criteria.true: Yes: the sentence asserts the relationship as true now or in the past.
criteria.false: No: the sentence denies it, conditions it, proposes it, forecasts it, or only reports that someone said it might happen.

mention_link.instructions: `mention_a` and `mention_b` are two mentions of an entity, each quoted with the surrounding sentence it appeared in. How do they relate?
criteria: They refer to two different real-world entities.
They refer to closely related entities that may or may not be the same one.
They refer to one and the same real-world entity.

same_name.instructions: Ignoring abbreviations, legal suffixes, honorifics and possessives, do `mention_a.text` and `mention_b.text` name the same thing?

record_link.instructions: Entity resolution: how do `entity_a` and `entity_b` relate?
criteria: They refer to two different real-world entities.
They refer to closely related entities that may or may not be the same one.
They refer to one and the same real-world entity.

relation.instructions: How do `a` and `b` relate to each other?

criteria.alternatives: Two options for the same role, such that adopting one usually means giving the other up: two package managers, two programming languages for the same job, two CI systems.
criteria.complementary: Different kinds of thing that are commonly held together and do not compete: a language and a database, a tool and a city.
criteria.same: Two names for one and the same thing.
criteria.unrelated: Nothing to do with each other.
